description: Stop doing arms wrong: leftovers, swing curls and once-a-week rumors. Retest your arm-to-waist ratio, then train your arm muscle signals instead with direct, frequent, strict work built for a light frame.

scenes.narration: Tape measure. | Arm flexed, cold. | Biggest point. | No pump allowed. | Waist at the navel. | Divide arm by waist. | That ratio is yours. | Write both numbers down. | Cold numbers only. | Warm numbers flatter. | At the end | I tell you | how arms get done right. | It is simpler than you think. | Pumped numbers do not count. | Cold tape only.

scenes.label: THE LINE THE OLD WAY NEVER CROSSES
scenes.narration: The line is zero point four five, arm-to-waist, where a light frame starts reading as athletic. If your ratio sits under zero point four zero, that number is the receipt for the old way: arms trained as leftovers, curls swung, forearms ignored, once a week at most. The old way is not a mystery and neither is its result. Done right looks different in every particular: direct work, strict form, high frequency, forearms included, measured cold and monthly. This episode replaces the old way piece by piece, and the replacement is smaller than you fear: ten focused minutes, three times a week, performed like you mean it. Small muscles do not need a bigger program. They need a correct one, repeated past the point where the old way would have quit.
scenes.sub: under 0.40: old way - over 0.50: arms own it

lines: the work and feel the limit.
beats.title: THE DIRECT RULE

beats.text: IF IT SWINGS, IT ISN'T SIGNAL

scenes.narration: The principle of done right, in one sentence: the target muscle must do the work, reach its limit, and know it was there. Direct means the biceps and forearms are the main event, not assistants at someone else's session. Strict means the load stays on the target through the whole range, especially the slow lowering phase, where a huge share of the growth signal is written and where swinging men donate their results to momentum. Training arm muscle signals instead of doing arm exercises is this distinction exactly. An exercise is a movement. A signal is tension delivered to a named muscle near its limit, repeatedly, on a schedule it can recover from and return to. Your arms have been present for hundreds of movements. They have received a few dozen signals. The ratio keeps the count, and the count is about to change. One more recruitment detail separates done right from the old way: the pause. A one-second squeeze at the top of the curl and a controlled three-second lowering turn a light load into a complete signal, because the muscle never gets a resting point inside the set. Momentum rests. Swinging rests. Done right never lets the target clock out mid-set, and the burn you feel is simply the sensation of a muscle that has finally been kept at work for its entire shift.

beats.text: CURL DAY / CARRY DAY / BOTH DAY

scenes.narration: The done-right week is almost disappointingly simple. Three arm sessions of about ten minutes. Day one, curls: towel curls or loaded curls, strict, slow negatives, sets near failure. Day two, forearms: farmer carries, dead hangs, towel hangs, the gripping work that builds the half of the arm the world actually sees. Day three, both, lighter, chasing perfect form and a deep burn. That is the entire architecture, and it outperforms the old way for a reason the split episode taught you: small muscles recover fast, so frequency is cheap, and signal density beats signal drama every time. Ten minutes fully owned beats forty minutes shared with your phone, your ego and three other muscle groups. Attach the sessions to days that already exist in your split and they will still be running in month six, which is when arm ratios actually move. And size the sessions to your life honestly. Ten minutes is the dose because ten minutes survives a bad day, a late meeting and a low mood, and a program that survives is the only kind that compounds. The man who needs forty perfect minutes trains arms twice a month. The man whose dose is ten trains them twelve times. Frequency is the active ingredient. Everything else is flavoring.

A word for the forearms, because done right treats them as headliners. In short sleeves and in every handshake, photograph and doorway, the forearm is the part of your arm on permanent display, and it responds to a kind of training curls cannot give it: sustained grip under load, time under tension measured in walks and hangs rather than reps. Carries build it because the forearm works isometrically at its limit for minutes, a signal density no curl set matches. This is also where your light frame cheats beautifully: your grip work doubles as tendon work, your hangs double as shoulder health, and the whole forearm program costs zero equipment beyond a towel and something heavy. The old way skipped forearms because they were not on the poster. Done right starts with them, because the poster was wrong about what people actually see.

beats.text: ADD REPS. ADD SECONDS. THEN LOAD.

scenes.narration: Progression, sized correctly for small muscles. Arms do not climb in five-kilo jumps; they climb in reps, in seconds of hang, in one more carry across the yard. Add a rep to the curl sets this week. Add five seconds to the hang next week. When the top of the rep range feels owned, then and only then add load. This small-print progression is why the logbook matters more for arms than for any other muscle: the gains are real but they are denominated in units memory rounds to zero. Write them and they compound visibly, which keeps you training, which compounds them further. The old way measured arms by feel and quit by feel. Done right measures by ink, and ink is undefeated against discouragement.
Train with me, done-right style. Four rounds, forty seconds of towel curls, three-second negatives, twenty seconds of rest. Every rep owned. This is the signal. Go.

Installation week. Put the three ten-minute sessions on your existing training days, curls, forearms, both. Start the log on page one with today's cold numbers. Choose loads your biceps choose, not your hips, and keep the negatives at three seconds even when the count suffers for it. The mistakes to leave behind permanently: the monthly hero arm day that soreness makes unforgettable and progress makes irrelevant. Measuring warm and calling it growth. And adding a fourth and fifth exercise when the first two, done strictly and logged, have not yet had their thirty days. Done right is not a bigger menu. It is a shorter one, executed like a professional, by a man whose ratio is done being patient.

beats.text: THE RATIO WILL INTRODUCE THE NEW ARMS

scenes.label: THEN THE COLD TAPE SPEAKS AGAIN
scenes.narration: So, your ratio. Under zero point four zero: the old way wrote this number, and thirty days of done-right work will be the first fair test your arms have ever had. Zero point four zero to zero point four five: the build zone, where frequency and strictness show up fastest, expect the tape to move at both ends. Over zero point four five: your arms are becoming the frame's headline, keep the rhythm and let the waist work widen the margin. Put your cold ratio in the comments. Just the number. In thirty days we measure cold again, same tape, same spot, and the new ratio will introduce your arms properly for the first time.
